objects.description: No custom types are defined in this header. It only includes other headers and sets up C linkage guards and include guards. Therefore, there are no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes defined here to document.

objects.definition: typedef struct AclContext_ *AclContext;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a library execution context. The underlying struct is not defined here; it is managed by the API and represents global state such as target/device selection, allocator, and configuration.

objects.definition: typedef struct AclQueue_ *AclQueue;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a submission/execution queue associated with a context. Represents command/tuning execution stream. Underlying definition is hidden.

objects.definition: typedef struct AclTensor_ *AclTensor;
objects.description: Opaque handle to a tensor resource managed by the library. Carries shape, layout, datatype and memory backing internally; definition is hidden.

objects.definition: typedef struct AclTensorPack_ *AclTensorPack;
objects.description: Opaque handle representing a collection/bundle of tensors (e.g., inputs/outputs for operators). Underlying structure is not exposed here.

objects.definition: typedef struct AclOperator_ *AclOperator;
objects.description: Opaque handle for a compute operator (e.g., convolution, activation). Encapsulates configured kernel(s). Structure is intentionally opaque.

objects.definition: typedef uint64_t AclTargetCapabilities;
objects.description: Bitfield describing enabled/available target capabilities for the context/backend. Values are backend-defined; multiple bits can be set.

objects.definition:
typedef enum AclStatus : int32_t
{
    AclSuccess            = 0,
    AclRuntimeError       = 1,
    AclOutOfMemory        = 2,
    AclUnimplemented      = 3,
    AclUnsupportedTarget  = 4,
    AclInvalidTarget      = 5,
    AclInvalidArgument    = 6,
    AclUnsupportedConfig  = 7,
    AclInvalidObjectState = 8,
} AclStatus;
objects.description: Enumeration of error/status codes returned by public API calls.
Enumeration of supported execution backends/targets.
Execution mode hint controlling optimization for repeated runs vs fast startup.

objects.definition:
typedef enum AclCpuCapabilities
{
    AclCpuCapabilitiesAuto = 0,
    AclCpuCapabilitiesNeon = (1 << 0),
    AclCpuCapabilitiesSve  = (1 << 1),
    AclCpuCapabilitiesSve2 = (1 << 2),
    AclCpuCapabilitiesFp16 = (1 << 7),
    AclCpuCapabilitiesBf16 = (1 << 8),
    AclCpuCapabilitiesDot      = (1 << 13),
    AclCpuCapabilitiesMmlaInt8 = (1 << 14),
    AclCpuCapabilitiesMmlaFp   = (1 << 15),
    AclCpuCapabilitiesAll = ~0
} AclCpuCapabilities;
objects.description: Bitmask enumeration of CPU feature toggles used to select optimized code paths.
Allocator interface callbacks that can be supplied to a context for custom memory management. The user populates function pointers and optional user_data.
Configuration struct for creating/configuring a context: execution mode, capabilities, fast-math toggle, kernel config path, max compute units, and an optional custom allocator.
Enumeration controlling autotuning aggressiveness for kernels.
Options for queue creation/configuration including tuning mode and the number of compute units to use.

objects.definition:
typedef enum AclDataType
{
    AclDataTypeUnknown = 0,
    AclUInt8           = 1,
    AclInt8            = 2,
    AclUInt16          = 3,
    AclInt16           = 4,
    AclUint32          = 5,
    AclInt32           = 6,
    AclFloat16         = 7,
    AclBFloat16        = 8,
    AclFloat32         = 9,
} AclDataType;
objects.description: Enumeration of supported scalar tensor element types.
Enumeration of supported data layouts for operations/tensors.
Enumeration indicating the origin/type of memory being imported into a tensor/resource. Currently only host pointers.
Public tensor metadata: number of dimensions, shape pointer, element data type, optional strides, and byte offset for the first element. Caller owns memory for shape/strides arrays.
Enumeration for identifying tensor slots when binding tensors to operators or packs (source, destination, vector).

objects.definition:
typedef enum
{
    AclActivationTypeNone = 0,  /**< No activation */
    AclIdentity           = 1,  /**< Identity */
    AclLogistic           = 2,  /**< Logistic */
    AclTanh               = 3,  /**< Hyperbolic tangent */
    AclRelu               = 4,  /**< Rectifier */
    AclBoundedRelu        = 5,  /**< Upper Bounded Rectifier */
    AclLuBoundedRelu      = 6,  /**< Lower and Upper Bounded Rectifier */
    AclLeakyRelu          = 7,  /**< Leaky Rectifier */
    AclSoftRelu           = 8,  /**< Soft Rectifier */
    AclElu                = 9,  /**< Exponential Linear Unit */
    AclAbs                = 10, /**< Absolute */
    AclSquare             = 11, /**< Square */
    AclSqrt               = 12, /**< Square root */
    AclLinear             = 13, /**< Linear */
    AclHardSwish          = 14, /**< Hard-swish */
} AclActivationType;
objects.description: Enumeration of supported activation function kinds for neural-network layers. Values include none/identity and common nonlinearities such as ReLU, bounded ReLU variants, logistic (sigmoid), tanh, ELU, HardSwish, etc. Used by AclActivationDescriptor.type.

Descriptor describing an activation layer configuration: the activation type plus optional scalar parameters a (alpha) and b (beta) used by certain activations (e.g., leaky ReLU slope, bounded limits, linear coefficients). The inplace flag hints that the operation may overwrite the input tensor. Construction is via aggregate initialization; no dedicated constructors are defined in this header.

Opaque handle type representing an execution context. Not defined in this header; it is referenced and expected to be defined in arm_compute/AclTypes.h. Purpose: holds internal state and options for kernels created under it.
Opaque handle type representing an operator execution/scheduling queue. Not defined in this header; referenced from arm_compute/AclTypes.h.
Opaque handle type for an N-dimensional tensor with optional backing memory. Not defined here; referenced from arm_compute/AclTypes.h.
Opaque handle type representing a collection of tensors to bind to operator slots. Not defined here; referenced from arm_compute/AclTypes.h.
Opaque handle type for an operator that can be executed on tensors. Not defined here; referenced from arm_compute/AclTypes.h.

Opaque handle type for an operator instance in the Arm Compute Library C API. This header references AclOperator via pointers and a macro cast, but its actual definition is not present here. Treat as an opaque type managed by the API.
Status/result code type used by API functions to report success or specific failure conditions. This header declares functions returning AclStatus but does not define the enum here.
Opaque handle to an execution/context object used when creating operators. Definition is not included in this header.
Descriptor type describing a tensor's metadata (shape, data type, layout, etc.). Only referenced here; actual struct/typedef definition is not in this header.
Descriptor for activation parameters (e.g., activation type and constants). Only referenced; definition provided elsewhere.
Holds semantic versioning metadata for the library, including major, minor, and patch numbers and an optional build information string. Intended to be returned by AclVersionInfo().

Status code enumeration type referenced by the API. It is not defined in this header; definition is expected in arm_compute/AclTypes.h. Purpose: convey success or error codes for ACL API calls. Details unknown in this header.
Opaque handle to a tensor object used by the ACL API. Not defined here; definition/typedef is expected in arm_compute/AclTypes.h. Represents an existing tensor managed elsewhere.

Descriptor structure describing a tensor’s properties (dimensions, data type, layout, etc.). Not defined here; definition is expected in arm_compute/AclTypes.h. Used as output parameter in AclGetTensorDescriptor.

objects.definition:
enum class StatusCode
{
    Success            = AclSuccess,
    RuntimeError       = AclRuntimeError,
    OutOfMemory        = AclOutOfMemory,
    Unimplemented      = AclUnimplemented,
    UnsupportedTarget  = AclUnsupportedTarget,
    InvalidArgument    = AclInvalidArgument,
    InvalidTarget      = AclInvalidTarget,
    UnsupportedConfig  = AclUnsupportedConfig,
    InvalidObjectState = AclInvalidObjectState,
};
objects.description: Strongly-typed status code enum mapping to the underlying C AclStatus values.
Execution target selection for context creation: CPU or OpenCL GPU.
Preference for runtime behavior: optimize for repeated runs or for startup latency.
High-level RAII wrapper around AclContext_ providing construction via AclCreateContext with customizable Options. Owns the underlying context and destroys it via ObjectDeleter specialization.
Nested options POD for Context creation, wrapping AclContextOptions and providing convenience constructors. Uses external types AclTargetCapabilities and AclAllocator.
Tuning effort level for operator scheduling and autotuning.
RAII wrapper for AclQueue_. Can be created from a Context with Options controlling tuning mode and scheduling units. Provides finish() to block until completion.
Nested options struct for Queue creation, wrapping AclQueueOptions.

objects.definition:
enum class DataType
{
    Unknown  = AclDataTypeUnknown,
    UInt8    = AclUInt8,
    Int8     = AclInt8,
    UInt16   = AclUInt16,
    Int16    = AclInt16,
    UInt32   = AclUint32,
    Int32    = AclInt32,
    Float16  = AclFloat16,
    BFloat16 = AclBFloat16,
    Float32  = AclFloat32,
};
objects.description: Element data types supported by tensors, mapping to the underlying C AclDataType.
C++ tensor descriptor wrapper building an AclTensorDescriptor from shape and DataType, or from an existing C descriptor. Stores shape and type; exposes get() to pass to C API.
Memory import type for Tensor::import; currently only host pointer is mapped.
RAII wrapper around AclTensor_. Supports creation (with optional allocation), mapping/unmapping, importing external memory, querying size and descriptor.
RAII wrapper for AclTensorPack_. Groups tensors with slot IDs for operator inputs/outputs. Provides convenience add overloads; contains nested PackPair helper struct.
Small helper to bundle a Tensor pointer with an operator slot ID for bulk addition into a TensorPack.
Base RAII wrapper for AclOperator_. Provides run() to enqueue execution on a Queue with a TensorPack. Constructed by derived operator classes via underlying C factory functions.
Concrete operator wrapping ACL activation operator creation via AclActivation. Inherits run() from Operator. ActivationDesc is a type alias to the C descriptor.

objects.definition: using ActivationDesc = AclActivationDescriptor;
objects.description: Alias to the C activation descriptor type. No definition here; it is a typedef alias within this header for convenience.

functions.name: AclCreateContext
functions.signature: AclStatus AclCreateContext(AclContext *ctx, AclTarget target, const AclContextOptions *options);
functions.description: Creates a new Arm Compute Library execution context for a given target, storing the resulting handle in ctx. Use the context to create and manage queues, tensors, and operators. Options configure defaults for kernels created under this context. Caller checks the returned status for success or specific failure reasons.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable storage for an AclContext handle.
target must be a supported AclTarget for the implementation, otherwise the function may return AclUnsupportedTarget.
options must be a pointer of type const AclContextOptions if provided; exact option fields and nullability are not specified in this header.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus and handle AclSuccess, AclOutOfMemory, AclUnsupportedTarget, or AclInvalidArgument.

functions.name: AclDestroyContext
functions.description: Destroys a previously created context and releases its resources. After successful return, the ctx handle must not be used.
requirements: ctx must be a valid context handle previously obtained from AclCreateContext.
Do not use ctx after a successful destruction.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus; may return AclInvalidArgument if the provided context is invalid.

functions.name: AclCreateQueue
functions.signature: AclStatus AclCreateQueue(AclQueue *queue, AclContext ctx, const AclQueueOptions *options);
functions.description: Creates an operator queue associated with the given context for scheduling operator execution. Stores the resulting queue handle in queue. Options control queue behavior.
requirements: queue must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable storage for an AclQueue handle.
ctx must be a valid context handle.
options must be a pointer of type const AclQueueOptions if provided; exact option fields and nullability are not specified in this header.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus and handle AclSuccess, AclOutOfMemory, AclUnsupportedTarget, or AclInvalidArgument.

functions.name: AclQueueFinish
functions.description: Blocks until all enqueued operations on the specified queue have completed. Use to synchronize host with device work submitted to the queue.
requirements: queue must be a valid queue handle created by AclCreateQueue.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus; may return AclInvalidArgument or AclRuntimeError.

functions.name: AclDestroyQueue
functions.description: Destroys a previously created queue and releases its resources. After successful return, the queue handle must not be used.
requirements: queue must be a valid queue handle.
Do not use the queue after a successful destruction.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus; may return AclInvalidArgument if the provided queue is invalid.

functions.name: AclCreateTensor
functions.signature: AclStatus AclCreateTensor(AclTensor *tensor, AclContext ctx, const AclTensorDescriptor *desc, bool allocate);
functions.description: Creates a tensor object with the provided descriptor within the given context. Optionally allocates backing memory immediately if allocate is true. The resulting tensor handle is written to tensor.
requirements: tensor must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable storage for an AclTensor handle.
ctx must be a valid context handle.
desc must be a valid pointer to an AclTensorDescriptor describing the tensor shape/format.
allocate selects whether backing memory should be allocated at creation; exact semantics beyond allocation are not detailed here.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus; may return AclOutOfMemory, AclUnsupportedTarget, or AclInvalidArgument.

functions.name: AclMapTensor
functions.description: Maps a tensor’s backing memory to host-accessible memory and returns a handle to that memory via handle. Use before direct host access; unmap with AclUnmapTensor when done.
requirements: tensor must be a valid tensor handle created by AclCreateTensor.
handle must be a valid, non-null pointer to receive the mapping handle (void*).
Caller must check the returned AclStatus; may return AclInvalidArgument.

functions.name: AclUnmapTensor
functions.description: Unmaps previously mapped tensor backing memory from the host. The handle should correspond to the mapping obtained from AclMapTensor (or the tensor’s current backing memory).
requirements: tensor must be a valid tensor handle.
handle must be a valid backing-memory handle corresponding to the specified tensor, typically obtained from AclMapTensor.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus; may return AclInvalidArgument.

functions.name: AclTensorImport
functions.signature: AclStatus AclTensorImport(AclTensor tensor, void *handle, AclImportMemoryType type);
functions.description: Imports external backing memory into the given tensor, allowing the tensor to use memory provided by the caller. The type indicates the memory import mechanism.
requirements: tensor must be a valid tensor handle.
handle must point to external memory suitable for the given import type; exact lifetime, alignment, and size requirements are not specified in this header.
type must be a valid AclImportMemoryType value.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus; may return AclInvalidArgument.

functions.name: AclDestroyTensor
functions.description: Destroys a tensor object and releases associated resources (and backing memory if owned). After successful return, the tensor handle must not be used.
requirements: tensor must be a valid tensor handle.
Do not use tensor after successful destruction.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus; may return AclInvalidArgument.

functions.name: AclCreateTensorPack
functions.description: Creates a tensor pack for grouping multiple tensors for operator execution. The resulting pack handle is written to pack.
requirements: pack must be a valid, non-null pointer to writable storage for an AclTensorPack handle.
ctx must be a valid context handle.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus; may return AclOutOfMemory or AclInvalidArgument.

functions.name: AclPackTensor
functions.signature: AclStatus AclPackTensor(AclTensorPack pack, AclTensor tensor, int32_t slot_id);
functions.description: Adds a single tensor to an existing tensor pack, associated with the specified operator slot identifier. Used to prepare inputs/outputs for operators.
requirements: pack must be a valid tensor pack handle created by AclCreateTensorPack.
tensor must be a valid tensor handle.
slot_id identifies the operator slot; valid range/values are not specified in this header.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus; may return AclOutOfMemory or AclInvalidArgument.

functions.name: AclPackTensors
functions.signature: AclStatus AclPackTensors(AclTensorPack pack, AclTensor *tensors, int32_t *slot_ids, size_t num_tensors);
functions.description: Adds multiple tensors to a tensor pack in one call, pairing each tensor with a slot ID. The number of entries to add is num_tensors.
requirements: pack must be a valid tensor pack handle.
tensors must be a valid, non-null pointer to an array of AclTensor handles with length at least num_tensors.
slot_ids must be a valid, non-null pointer to an array of int32_t with length at least num_tensors.
num_tensors specifies how many entries to pack; must match the accessible lengths of tensors and slot_ids.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus; may return AclOutOfMemory or AclInvalidArgument.

functions.name: AclDestroyTensorPack
functions.description: Destroys a tensor pack and releases associated resources. After successful return, the pack handle must not be used.
requirements: pack must be a valid tensor pack handle.
Do not use the pack after a successful destruction.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus; may return AclInvalidArgument.

functions.name: AclRunOperator
functions.signature: AclStatus AclRunOperator(AclOperator op, AclQueue queue, AclTensorPack tensors);
functions.description: Executes an operator eagerly on the provided inputs/outputs contained in tensors, scheduling work on queue. Use to run an operator without building a larger graph.
requirements: op must be a valid operator handle.
queue must be a valid queue handle.
tensors must be a valid tensor pack containing the tensors and slot mappings expected by the operator; exact slot semantics are not specified here.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus; may return AclOutOfMemory, AclUnsupportedTarget, AclInvalidArgument, or AclRuntimeError.

functions.name: AclDestroyOperator
functions.description: Destroys an operator object and releases its resources. After successful return, the operator handle must not be used.
requirements: op must be a valid operator handle.
Do not use op after a successful destruction.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus; may return AclInvalidArgument.

functions.name: AclActivation
functions.signature: AclStatus AclActivation(AclOperator *op, AclContext ctx, const AclTensorDescriptor *src, const AclTensorDescriptor *dst, const AclActivationDescriptor info);
functions.description: Creates an activation operator that applies the specified activation function to a tensor. Intended usage: provide a valid context, source and destination tensor descriptors, and activation metadata; on success, an operator handle is returned via op. Can be used to validate support by passing the special operator value ARM_COMPUTE_VALIDATE_OPERATOR_SUPPORT (no operator is created). Supported backends include OpenCL (ClActivationLayer) and CPU (CpuActivationLayer).
requirements: Caller must inspect the returned AclStatus and handle errors (AclSuccess, AclOutOfMemory, AclUnsupportedTarget, AclInvalidArgument).

If only validating operator support, pass op = ARM_COMPUTE_VALIDATE_OPERATOR_SUPPORT; otherwise op should be a valid non-null pointer to receive the created operator handle. (From macro comment in this header.)
ctx must be a valid AclContext created/initialized by the library before this call. (Inferred from type and typical usage.)
src must point to an initialized AclTensorDescriptor describing the input tensor (slot ACL_SRC).
dst must point to an initialized AclTensorDescriptor describing the output tensor (slot ACL_DST).
info must be a valid AclActivationDescriptor describing the activation type and parameters expected by that type.
Element-wise operation is implied; dst is expected to be shape/type compatible with src for the chosen activation (inferred; exact constraints are not explicitly documented).
The chosen target/backend must support the combination of tensor descriptors and activation type; otherwise AclUnsupportedTarget may be returned.

functions.name: AclGetClContext
functions.description: Returns the underlying OpenCL cl_context associated with a Compute Library AclContext that uses the OpenCL backend. Use this to interoperate with raw OpenCL APIs. Note: This header does not specify ownership or refcounting behavior for the returned cl_context; callers should treat it as an external handle managed by the library. The function returns an AclStatus indicating success or failure.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-zero AclContext for the OpenCL backend.
opencl_context must be a non-null pointer to storage for the resulting cl_context.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus and handle errors appropriately.

functions.name: AclGetClDevice
functions.description: Returns the underlying OpenCL cl_device_id used by a Compute Library AclContext that targets the OpenCL backend. Enables device-level interop with OpenCL. Ownership/refcounting of the returned cl_device_id is unspecified by this header.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-zero AclContext for the OpenCL backend.
opencl_device must be a non-null pointer to storage for the resulting cl_device_id.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus and handle errors appropriately.

functions.name: AclSetClContext
functions.description: Sets the underlying OpenCL cl_context to be used by a Compute Library AclContext that targets the OpenCL backend, enabling the library to interoperate with an application-provided OpenCL context. Note: The parameter is an input despite a conflicting @param[out] tag in the comment.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, non-zero AclContext for the OpenCL backend.
opencl_context must be a valid OpenCL cl_context handle.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus and handle errors appropriately.

functions.name: AclGetClQueue
functions.description: Returns the underlying OpenCL cl_command_queue associated with a Compute Library AclQueue that uses the OpenCL backend, for interop with raw OpenCL command queue operations. Ownership/refcounting of the returned cl_command_queue is unspecified by this header.
requirements: queue must be a valid, non-zero AclQueue for the OpenCL backend.
The AclQueue refcount must be 0 (i.e., not used by other objects) at the time of the call.
opencl_queue must be a non-null pointer to storage for the resulting cl_command_queue.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus and handle errors appropriately.

functions.name: AclSetClQueue
functions.description: Sets the underlying OpenCL cl_command_queue to be used by a Compute Library AclQueue targeting the OpenCL backend, allowing the library to use an application-created command queue. Note: The parameter is an input despite a conflicting @param[out] tag in the comment; the comment also contains a typo (opecl_queue).
requirements: queue must be a valid, non-zero AclQueue for the OpenCL backend.
opencl_queue must be a valid OpenCL cl_command_queue handle.
opencl_queue must be created from the same OpenCL context as the AclContext that the AclQueue will use.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus and handle errors appropriately.

functions.name: AclGetClMem
functions.description: Returns the underlying OpenCL cl_mem object backing a Compute Library AclTensor, enabling OpenCL interop for buffer/image access. Ownership/refcounting of the returned cl_mem is unspecified by this header.
requirements: tensor must be a valid, non-zero AclTensor.
opencl_mem must be a non-null pointer to storage for the resulting cl_mem.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus and handle errors appropriately.

functions.name: AclVersionInfo
functions.description: Returns a pointer to read-only semantic version metadata for the library, including major, minor, patch, and build_info fields. Typical usage: call at runtime to query the library version for logging, diagnostics, or feature gating. Details about lifetime or thread-safety are not documented here; based on the const return type and common patterns, the data should be treated as static, read-only metadata.
requirements: No arguments are required.
Do not modify the returned AclVersion contents (the pointer is to const data).
Do not free or otherwise take ownership of the returned pointer; treat it as a borrowed read-only pointer.
Behavior on NULL return is not documented; callers should defensively check for NULL if robustness is required (inferred due to lack of explicit guarantees).

functions.name: AclGetTensorSize
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the given tensor as computed from its descriptor (dimensions, data type, etc.), not from its allocated memory. Typical usage: pass a valid tensor handle and a writable uint64_t pointer; on success, *size is set and AclSuccess is returned. Use the result to plan memory usage or validate layouts.
requirements: tensor must reference an existing/valid tensor handle (inferred from parameter name and documentation).
size must be a non-null pointer to writable memory of type uint64_t.
The tensor must have a valid descriptor from which size can be derived; otherwise the call will fail with AclInvalidArgument (inferred from description and return codes).
Caller must check the returned AclStatus and handle AclInvalidArgument on invalid input.

functions.name: AclGetTensorDescriptor
functions.description: Retrieves the descriptor of the specified tensor and writes it to the caller-provided AclTensorDescriptor. Use this to inspect tensor properties such as dimensions and data type.
requirements: tensor must reference an existing/valid tensor handle (inferred from parameter name and documentation).
desc must be a non-null pointer to writable memory of type AclTensorDescriptor.
Caller must check the returned AclStatus and handle AclInvalidArgument on invalid input.

functions.name: acl::detail::as_cenum
functions.signature:
template <typename E, typename SE>
constexpr E acl::detail::as_cenum(SE v) noexcept
functions.description: Converts a strongly-typed enum value (SE) to its corresponding plain C-style enum type (E) by casting through the underlying integral type. Intended for bridging between C++ enums and C APIs.
requirements: Template parameter E must be an enum type compatible with the target C API.
Template parameter SE must be an enum (strongly-typed) whose underlying value maps to E.
Function is constexpr and noexcept; it must be usable in constant expressions.

functions.name: acl::detail::as_enum
functions.signature:
template <typename SE, typename E>
constexpr SE acl::detail::as_enum(E val) noexcept
functions.description: Converts a plain C-style enum value (E) to a strongly-typed enum (SE) using static_cast. Used to wrap C API enum values into C++ enum classes.
requirements: Template parameter SE must be a strongly-typed enum compatible with the C value E.
Template parameter E must be an enum whose values map to SE.
Function is constexpr and noexcept; it must be usable in constant expressions.

functions.name: acl::operator==
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
bool acl::detail::operator==(const acl::detail::ObjectBase<T> &lhs, const acl::detail::ObjectBase<T> &rhs)
functions.description: Compares two library object wrappers for equality by comparing their underlying handles/pointers. Returns true if both wrappers refer to the same underlying object (including both being null).
requirements: Both lhs and rhs must be ObjectBase wrappers over the same template parameter T.
No additional preconditions; null handles are allowed and compare equal if both null.

functions.name: acl::operator!=
functions.signature:
template <typename T>
bool acl::detail::operator!=(const acl::detail::ObjectBase<T> &lhs, const acl::detail::ObjectBase<T> &rhs)
functions.description: Inequality comparison for library object wrappers. Returns true if the underlying handles/pointers differ.
requirements: Both lhs and rhs must be ObjectBase wrappers over the same template parameter T.
No additional preconditions; null handles are allowed.

functions.name: acl::report_status
functions.signature: static inline void acl::report_status(acl::StatusCode status, const std::string &msg)
functions.description: Reports a status code. When exceptions are enabled at build time, throws acl::Status if status != Success; otherwise it performs no-op logging suppression. Used to propagate failures from C API calls.
requirements: Caller must be prepared for an exception to be thrown when exceptions are enabled and status is not Success.
The msg parameter may be ignored when exceptions are disabled.
No return value; use the thrown exception or prior status variable for error handling.

functions.name: acl::Context::Context
functions.description: Constructs a compute context for the specified target using default conservative options. Internally calls AclCreateContext and stores the resulting handle. May throw via report_status on failure when exceptions are enabled.
requirements: target must be a valid acl::Target supported by the runtime.
If status is non-null, it will be set to the result of the creation call.
On failure and when exceptions are enabled, an exception is thrown; otherwise the caller must check the status out-parameter if provided.

functions.name: acl::Queue::Queue
functions.description: Creates a scheduling/tuning queue from the given context using default queue options. May throw via report_status on failure when exceptions are enabled.
requirements: ctx must be a valid, successfully created Context.
If status is non-null, it will be set to the result of the creation call.
On failure and when exceptions are enabled, an exception is thrown; otherwise the caller must check the status out-parameter if provided.

functions.name: acl::Queue::finish
functions.description: Blocks until all tasks enqueued on this queue have completed. Wraps AclQueueFinish and returns the resulting status.
requirements: This queue must be valid.
Caller should check the returned StatusCode for success or failure.

functions.name: acl::TensorDescriptor::TensorDescriptor
functions.description: Constructs a tensor descriptor from a shape and data type. The descriptor sets ndims, shape pointer, data type, and clears strides and byte offset.
requirements: shape defines the tensor dimensions; maximum supported dimensionality is 6 (as noted for tensors).
data_type selects the element data type.
The provided shape vector must outlive the temporary use during construction; internally a copy of shape is stored, so post-construction lifetime of the input is not required.

functions.name: acl::TensorDescriptor::get
functions.description: Returns a pointer to the underlying C AclTensorDescriptor for interop with the C API.
requirements: The returned pointer remains valid as long as this TensorDescriptor object remains alive and unmodified.
Do not store the pointer beyond the lifetime of the descriptor.

functions.name: acl::TensorDescriptor::operator==
functions.description: Compares two tensor descriptors for equality by checking data type and exact shape equality (same rank and per-dimension sizes).
requirements: other must be a valid TensorDescriptor.
Equality is defined strictly on data type and shape; other fields (e.g., strides, offsets) are not considered in this implementation.

functions.name: acl::Tensor::Tensor
functions.description: Creates a tensor with memory allocated, using the provided context and descriptor. Delegates to the allocating constructor with allocate=true. May throw via report_status on failure when exceptions are enabled.
requirements: ctx must be a valid Context.
desc must describe a valid tensor (dimensions and type).
If status is non-null, it will be set to the result of the creation call.
On failure and when exceptions are enabled, an exception is thrown; otherwise the caller must check the status out-parameter if provided.

functions.name: acl::Tensor::map
functions.description: Maps the tensor’s backing memory for host access and returns a host pointer on success, or nullptr on failure. Wraps AclMapTensor and reports errors via report_status.
requirements: This tensor must be valid and, if required by the backend, allocated or properly imported.
Caller must call unmap(handle) with the returned handle when host access is no longer needed.
On failure and when exceptions are enabled, an exception may be thrown; otherwise a nullptr may be returned and status was reported.

functions.name: acl::Tensor::unmap
functions.description: Unmaps a previously mapped tensor memory handle obtained from map(). Wraps AclUnmapTensor.
requirements: handle must be a value previously returned by this tensor’s map() call.
Caller must check the returned StatusCode for success or failure.

functions.name: acl::Tensor::import
functions.description: Imports externally owned memory into the tensor according to the specified import type (e.g., host pointer). Wraps AclTensorImport and binds the external buffer to the tensor.
requirements: handle must be a valid external memory handle compatible with the tensor’s descriptor (size and layout) inferred from the operation’s purpose.
type must specify a supported import memory type (currently Host).
Caller must check the returned StatusCode for success or failure.

functions.name: acl::Tensor::get_size
functions.description: Returns the size in bytes of the tensor as implied by its descriptor (shape and data type), not the actual allocated size. Wraps AclGetTensorSize.
requirements: Tensor must be valid.
Caller should assume the size is derived from descriptor metadata, not actual allocation.

functions.name: acl::Tensor::get_descriptor
functions.description: Retrieves the tensor’s descriptor from the underlying C API and returns it as a C++ TensorDescriptor wrapper. Wraps AclGetTensorDescriptor.
requirements: Tensor must be valid.
On internal failure and when exceptions are enabled, an exception may be thrown; otherwise caller should use the resulting object accordingly.

functions.name: acl::TensorPack::TensorPack
functions.description: Constructs an empty tensor pack associated with a context. Used to group tensors and their slot IDs for operator execution. May throw via report_status on failure when exceptions are enabled.
requirements: ctx must be a valid Context.
If status is non-null, it will be set to the result of the creation call.
On failure and when exceptions are enabled, an exception is thrown; otherwise the caller must check the status out-parameter if provided.

functions.name: acl::TensorPack::add
functions.description: Adds a single tensor to the pack with the specified slot ID, to match the operator’s expected inputs. Wraps AclPackTensor.
requirements: tensor must be a valid Tensor.
slot_id should correspond to a valid operator slot (operator-defined).
Caller must check the returned StatusCode for success or failure.

functions.name: acl::Operator::run
functions.description: Executes the operator on the provided queue using the given tensor pack as inputs/outputs according to the operator’s slot conventions. Wraps AclRunOperator.
requirements: queue must be a valid Queue created from a compatible Context.
pack must contain tensors bound to the correct slot IDs expected by this operator.
Caller must check the returned StatusCode for success or failure.

functions.name: acl::Activation::Activation
functions.signature: acl::Activation::Activation(acl::Context &ctx, const acl::TensorDescriptor &src, const acl::TensorDescriptor &dst, const acl::ActivationDesc &desc, acl::StatusCode *status = nullptr)
functions.description: Constructs an Activation operator configured with source and destination tensor descriptors and an activation descriptor (type/parameters). Wraps AclActivation. May throw via report_status on failure when exceptions are enabled.
requirements: ctx must be a valid Context.
src and dst must describe compatible shapes/data types for the chosen activation; specifics depend on the activation algorithm.
desc must be a valid AclActivationDescriptor initialized per the C API.
If status is non-null, it will be set to the result of the creation call.
On failure and when exceptions are enabled, an exception is thrown; otherwise the caller must check the status out-parameter if provided.
